_schema: key -> {label, value (display text, used verbatim in copy), tag (M measured/documented, C calculated, I illustrative), num (optional number in SI or stated unit), unit (optional), note (optional), source (short citation), url}. Copy refers to a fact as {{key}}.

date_time.label: Date and time
date_time.note: Mountain War Time = UTC-6 (11:29:45 UTC). 05:29:45 is the widely used official time (LANL, US Army, NPS). Some later accounts give 05:29:21 +/- 15 s, and a 2023 seismic estimate is about 05:29:24; the radio timing signal failed. Show 05:29:45 and call it 'about'.
date_time.source: LANL National Security Science 'The Trinity Test' (2020); US Army 80th-anniversary series; Atomic Archive NPS text

place.label: Place
place.note: Alamogordo Bombing Range (Groves's 1945 memo says 'Alamogordo Air Base'); now White Sands Missile Range.
place.source: Groves memo to Sec. of War, 18 Jul 1945 (FRUS); NPS White Sands

tower_height.label: Tower height
tower_height.source: LANL 'The Trinity Test'; Wikipedia Trinity (nuclear test)

shelter_dist.label: Observer shelters
shelter_dist.note: North, west and south shelters (N-10,000, W-10,000, S-10,000). The control shelter was the south one.

base_camp_dist.label: Base camp
base_camp_dist.note: 10 miles southwest per Fermi's account; an NPS nomination form says 11 miles. The main VIP observation point was 17,000 yd (15.5 km) away (Groves).

detonators.label: Detonators and lenses
detonators.note: Confirmed: the Wikipedia Fat Man article says the Y-1561 model, which the Trinity Gadget used, had 32 detonators starting a detonation wave in each of 32 tapered high-explosive columns (the same article also gives a different count elsewhere, so the number rests on the standard accounts).
detonators.source: Wikipedia 'Fat Man'; standard accounts (Rhodes; Atomic Archive)

core_mass.label: Plutonium core
core_mass.note: about the size of an orange. Sources give 6.1 to 6.19 kg; 6.2 is fine as a rounded figure.
core_mass.source: Wikipedia Trinity (6.19 kg); Brookings 'The Gadget' (orange, 6.1 kg); Atomic Archive core photo caption (6.2 kg)

layers.label: Layers, outside in
layers.value: detonators, explosive lenses, inner charge, aluminium pusher, natural-uranium tamper, plutonium core, polonium-beryllium initiator
layers.note: Checked against the Wikipedia Fat Man article: lenses (fast Composition B outside, slow Baratol inside), aluminium pusher, tamper (the article says both depleted and natural uranium; Trinity's is usually described as natural uranium), plutonium pit, polonium-beryllium initiator. The article also lists a thin boron-plastic shell between pusher and tamper, left out of the schematic. The 'inner charge' layer is a simplification of the Baratol shell.
layers.source: Wikipedia 'Fat Man'; standard accounts (Rhodes; Atomic Archive)

compression.label: Peak compression
compression.value: more than 2× normal density, at about 60 µs

mev_per_fission.label: Energy per fission
mev_per_fission.note: 200 MeV = 3.204e-11 J. About 180 MeV is promptly available; the rest comes later from fission-product decay.
mev_per_fission.source: Glasstone & Dolan, Effects of Nuclear Weapons, 1977, sec. 1.43-1.45

neutrons_per_fission.label: Neutrons per fission
neutrons_per_fission.note: Pu-239: about 2.9 (2.88) for slow neutrons, about 3.0 for fast neutrons. Standard nuclear data; not re-fetched in this pass.
neutrons_per_fission.source: Standard nuclear data (ENDF/B); Glasstone & Dolan ch. 1

generation_time.label: Generation time
generation_time.note: One shake is defined as 10 ns. Using it as the generation time is the usual popular order-of-magnitude figure; the true value in the compressed core is a few ns. Could not find a primary source for a precise number.

generations.label: Generations
generations.note: 2^81 = 2.42e24 fissions in total; 21 kt needs 2.74e24 (about 81.4 doublings). 'About 80' is the usual popular figure. The last 7 doublings release 1 - 2^-7 = 99.2% of the energy.

yield_kt.label: Yield used here
yield_kt.note: Official figure since the 1963 revision by Los Alamos and the AEC (not a 1945 number). 1 kt = 4.184e12 J.

yield_fermi.label: Fermi's paper scraps
yield_fermi.note: Fermi dropped scraps from about 6 ft (fermi_drop_height); they shifted about 2.5 m (fermi_displacement); both confirmed in his own account. His own account says about 10,000 tons. A blast-gauge measurement of 9.9 +/- 1.0 kt is also quoted on Wikipedia (primary not checked).

yield_1945.label: 1945 radiochemistry
yield_1945.note: The original range '18.6 to 21 kt' mixed two dates. Groves's memo of 18 July 1945 estimated 'in excess of 15,000 to 20,000 tons'.

yield_2021.label: 2021 re-analysis
yield_2021.note: Selby et al., Los Alamos, trinitite samples with modern mass spectrometry; Nuclear Technology 207 (sup1), Dec 2021, pp. S321-S325. Reported publicly in 2022.
yield_2021.source: Selby et al., Nucl. Technol. 207 (2021); arXiv:2103.06258; LANL 1663

pu_fissioned.label: Plutonium fissioned
pu_fissioned.note: 2.74e24 fissions x 239.05 u (3.97e-25 kg) = 1.09 kg; 1.09/6.19 = 17.6%. Caveat: part of the 21 kt came from fast fission of the uranium tamper (Wikipedia: about 15 kt core, 6 kt tamper; primary not checked), so plutonium alone was less (about 0.8 kg). Say 'about 1 kg of material fissioned'.
pu_fissioned.source: Own arithmetic; Glasstone Table 1.45 (1.45e23 fissions per kt at 180 MeV gives 1.2 kg)

core_temp.label: Core temperature at peak
core_temp.note: Order of magnitude; standard textbook figure, not re-fetched.

shock_law.label: Blast-wave radius
shock_law.note: Taylor-Sedov with the constant taken as 1. The exact constant for gamma=1.4 is 1.033, but with 21 kt and rho=1.2 kg/m3 the constant 1 reproduces Taylor's measured radii to about 1% for t = 0.4-2 ms and 2-5% high for 3-62 ms. Using 1.033 gives 140 m at 25 ms (8% high). Do not print the constant. Trinity air is about 1.0-1.1 kg/m3 at the site altitude; 1.2 is the sea-level value and is kept because it fits.
shock_law.source: Taylor, Proc. Roy. Soc. A 201 (1950) 159 and 175; Wikipedia Taylor-von Neumann-Sedov blast wave; own fit

shock_r_25ms.label: Radius at 25 ms
shock_r_25ms.note: (8.786e13 x 6.25e-4 / 1.2)^0.2 = 135.6 m. Taylor's measured value at 25 ms is 130 m.

fireball_r_vs_t.label: Measured fireball/shock radius against time
fireball_r_vs_t.value: 25 points from 0.10 ms (11.1 m) to 62 ms (185 m)
fireball_r_vs_t.note: Taylor's Table 1, read from Mack's film. Log-log slope fitted for t >= 3 ms is 0.39 (theory 0.40). Points below about 0.4 ms sit below the 2/5 line (the blast is not yet self-similar). Transcription from a course data file; re-check against the paper before publishing. Second-source check: Taylor's own text and arXiv:2403.19657 confirm the photographs came from Mack's film (time stamps from 0.10 ms), but neither tabulates the radii in text form, so this transcription rests on one data file.
fireball_r_vs_t.source: Taylor, Proc. Roy. Soc. A 201 (1950) 175-186, Table 1 (via Univ. of Connecticut data file)

fireball_r_interp.label: Interpolated radii at the listed stamps
fireball_r_interp.value: 6 ms: about 74 m; 16 ms: about 109 m; 90 ms: about 215 m (extrapolated)
fireball_r_interp.note: Not measured by Taylor. 6 ms and 16 ms are interpolated on the t^0.4 trend between his points; 90 ms is extrapolated beyond his last point (62 ms) and scaled by his 0.95 offset (formula alone gives 226 m).

photo_times.label: Photograph times
photo_times.value: 15, 25, 34, 53 and 62 ms (Taylor's table); a 16 ms frame is the best-known published image
photo_times.note: Of the original list 6, 16, 25, 53, 62, 90 ms: 25, 53 and 62 ms are in Taylor's table; 16 ms is a published LANL frame (PA-98-0520); a frame described as about 6 ms circulates; no source found for 90 ms and Taylor's table stops at 62 ms. Recommend stamping 15, 25, 34, 53, 62 ms, or marking 6 and 90 ms as 'on the same line' rather than 'Mack frames'.
photo_times.source: Taylor (1950) Table 1; Wikimedia Commons 'Trinity Test Fireball 16ms'; Fstoppers

breakaway_time.label: Shock breakaway (20 kt)
breakaway_time.note: Glasstone sec. 2.120: breakaway at about 0.015 s for a 20 kt weapon (free air). The minimum luminosity is at about 11 ms. A ground-level shot like Trinity keeps a luminous front somewhat longer; Mack's frames still show the bright edge on the t^0.4 line to 62 ms. Safe to fade the front between 15 and about 60 ms.

breakaway_radius.label: Radius at breakaway
breakaway_radius.note: Glasstone: R = 100 W^0.4 ft for an air burst (101 m at 20 kt) and 145 W^0.4 ft for a contact surface burst (146 m). Taylor measured 106.5 m at 15 ms. Trinity (100 ft tower) lies between: 100-145 m.

fireball_max_radius.label: Maximum fireball radius
fireball_max_radius.value: about 235 m, reached after roughly a second
fireball_max_radius.note: Glasstone: maximum is about twice the breakaway radius (200-290 m); the older table gives a maximum fireball diameter of 1,550 ft for a 20 kt air burst (radius 236 m). The glow is gone by about 10 s.
fireball_max_radius.source: Glasstone & Dolan 1977, sec. 2.121; Fig. 2.51 as transcribed at abomb1.org

thermal_max2_time.label: Second thermal maximum
thermal_max2_time.note: t_max = 0.0417 W^0.44 s (1977 edition, bursts below 15,000 ft) = 0.156 s at 20 kt, 0.16 s at 21 kt. Apparent surface temperature about 7,700 C at that point. The second pulse carries about 99% of the thermal energy.

blast_base_camp.label: Blast reaches base camp
blast_base_camp.note: Fermi: 'about 40 seconds' at base camp (10 miles); Groves: 'about forty seconds' at 17,000 yd. Straight sound travel at 340 m/s over 16 km is 47 s, so 40 s is an eyewitness figure; the sim may give 43-47 s.

blast_shelter.label: Blast reaches the 9.1 km shelters
blast_shelter.note: 9,144 m / 340 m/s = 26.9 s, minus a second or so for the faster early shock. No measured value found.

cloud_top.label: Cloud top
cloud_top.value: about 12 km above sea level (about 11 km above the ground)
cloud_top.note: Sources: Groves 41,000 ft above sea level = 36,000 ft above ground (12.5 km); NPS/LANL 38,000 ft (11.6 km); Bethe 40,000 ft above ground; Fermi's early guess 30,000 ft. The site is about 1.4 km above sea level. Recommend 12 km.

cloud_rise_time.label: Time to reach cloud top
cloud_rise_time.note: Groves: 41,000 ft 'in about five minutes'; NPS: 38,000 ft within seven minutes. Bethe: early rise about 120 m/s. Cloud stabilises at about 10 minutes (Glasstone, general). Recommend 300 s to the top, with the scene ending at 600 s.
cloud_rise_time.source: Groves memo (FRUS); NPS; Bethe account (Atomic Archive)

crater.label: Crater
crater.value: shallow: about 1.4 to 1.8 m deep, about 40 to 80 m across
crater.note: Sources disagree: Groves 1945 'shallow bowl 130 ft across, 6 ft deep' (40 m, 1.8 m); Wikipedia 1.4 m deep, 80 m wide; NPS and others quote 8 ft deep and 'half a mile', which refers to the whole scoured, glassed area. In copy say 'shallow'.

trinitite_extent.label: Glass (trinitite) out to
trinitite_extent.note: Radius about 330 yd (300 m) per Wikipedia; consistent with the 'half mile' wide scoured area quoted by NPS.

split_blast.label: Blast share
split_blast.note: Air-burst rule of thumb (Glasstone sec. 1.25-1.26), shares of total fission energy including later decay energy. Trinity was a low shot with a crater, so more went into ground shock and dust and less into heat. Suggested caption: 'Typical split for an air burst; Trinity was low, so its split differed.'

split_heat.label: Heat share
split_heat.note: Air burst: 35%. Contact surface burst: effective thermal fraction about 18% (Glasstone sec. 7.101; table range 0.19-0.35 for other surface bursts).

split_radiation.label: Nuclear radiation share
split_radiation.note: 5% initial (first minute) plus 10% residual (fission-product decay over time). The stated yield (21 kt) excludes the residual part, so against the 21 kt the shares are about 56% blast, 39% heat, 6% prompt radiation.

fallout_note.label: Fallout
fallout_note.value: heaviest off-site fallout about 48 km (30 miles) from ground zero; nearby residents were not warned or evacuated
fallout_note.note: Cattle on ranches were marked by beta burns (the Army bought 88). A 2020 dose reconstruction names Guadalupe, Lincoln, San Miguel, Socorro and Torrance counties as most contaminated. New Mexico downwinders were added to the Radiation Exposure Compensation Act in July 2025.

nagasaki_date.label: Nagasaki
nagasaki_date.note: 24 days after Trinity; same plutonium implosion design (Fat Man). Say '24 days later' or 'less than four weeks later', not 'three weeks'.

fermi_drop_height.label: Height of Fermi's paper drop
fermi_drop_height.note: Fermi: 'from about six feet small pieces of paper'.
fermi_drop_height.source: Fermi's own account of the test (Dannen archive)

fermi_displacement.label: Displacement of Fermi's paper scraps
fermi_displacement.source: Fermi's own account of the test (Dannen archive)
